day_by_day.morning: Arrival — Flight KL lands at 13:00, so no morning activities. Take the Amsterdam Airport Express (Sprinter train) from Schiphol to Amsterdam Centraal (~17 min, €5.40). Check in to Canal House Amsterdam and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Orientation canal walk: Stroll along the Herengracht, Keizersgracht, and Prinsengracht canals near the hotel to get your bearings. Explore the Jordaan neighbourhood — browse free street art, peek into courtyards (hofjes), and window-shop along Haarlemmerdijk. Completely free and a perfect soft introduction to Amsterdam.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Leidseplein area for a relaxed evening. Explore the lively square, grab a drink at a brown café (bruine kroeg) and soak up the local atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack on arrival at Schiphol — try a broodje (Dutch sandwich roll) from one of the airport bakeries (~€4).
meals.lunch: FEBO automat on the way from Centraal Station — iconic Dutch fast food (kroket or frikandel) for under €3. Quick, cheap, and authentically Dutch.
meals.dinner: Foodhallen (covered food market in Oud-West, ~20 min by tram) — choose from multiple affordable stalls. Budget €10–14 for a satisfying meal and a local beer.

day_by_day.notes: Buy a multi-day GVB transit card at Centraal Station (3-day card ~€17.50) to cover trams and buses for the next few days. Validate it every time you board. Keep luggage light on Day 1 — you'll be navigating public transport from the airport.

day_by_day.morning: Rijksmuseum Visit — Doors open at 09:00; arrive early to beat crowds. Explore the Netherlands' premier art and history museum, home to masterpieces by Rembrandt (The Night Watch) and Vermeer (The Milkmaid). Plan 2.5–3 hours. Book tickets online in advance to save time (€22.50 adult). The museum gardens (Museumplein) are free to enter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Van Gogh Museum Experience — Located just 200 m from the Rijksmuseum on Museumplein. Discover the world's largest collection of Van Gogh's works including Sunflowers and The Bedroom. Book timed-entry tickets online in advance (€22). Spend 1.5–2 hours. Afterwards, relax on the Museumplein lawn — a favourite local hangout.
day_by_day.evening: Walk or tram to the De Pijp neighbourhood. Browse the Albert Cuypmarkt (closes ~18:00 on Saturdays) for cheap snacks and Dutch stroopwafels. Explore the lively streets and end the evening with a canal-side sit-down.

meals.breakfast: Grab fresh bread and cheese from a local Albert Heijn supermarket near the hotel (~€3–5). Eat in or take to a canal bench.
meals.lunch: Broodje Bert or a similar sandwich shop near Museumplein — hearty Dutch sandwiches for €5–7.
meals.dinner: Warung Spang Makandra in De Pijp — excellent Surinamese-Javanese food, huge portions, very budget-friendly (~€10–13). A true Amsterdam institution.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday museums can be very busy — pre-booked timed-entry tickets for both the Rijksmuseum and Van Gogh Museum are essential. Doing both museums on the same day saves travel time since they are side by side. Wear comfortable shoes — lots of walking today.

day_by_day.morning: Anne Frank House Tour — One of Amsterdam's most moving and important sites. Walk through the hidden annex where Anne Frank and her family hid during WWII. Tickets MUST be booked online weeks in advance (€16); walk-up tickets are virtually impossible to get. Arrive at your timed slot (aim for 09:00–10:00 opening slot). Allow 1.5 hours. The house is a short walk from Canal House Amsterdam.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private Canal Boat Tour — After the emotional morning, enjoy a lighter afternoon gliding through Amsterdam's UNESCO-listed canal ring on a guided boat tour, passing iconic 17th-century merchant houses, drawbridges, and houseboats. Several operators depart near the Westerkerk/Anne Frank House area. Look for shared group tours (~€15–18) rather than private charters to keep costs down. Duration: ~1 hour.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the Jordaan neighbourhood — Amsterdam's most charming district of narrow streets, independent boutiques, and cosy cafés. Visit the Noordermarkt area and wind down with a drink at a traditional bruine kroeg.

meals.breakfast: Café Winkel 43 near Noordermarkt — famous for their apple pie. A slice + coffee ~€7. A beloved local Sunday morning ritual.
meals.lunch: Pick up fresh stroopwafels, herring (haring), and snacks from a street stall near the canal (~€5–7 total). Eat by the water.
meals.dinner: Moeders restaurant in Jordaan — hearty traditional Dutch home cooking in a cosy, quirky setting. Mains around €14–17. Book ahead as it fills up on Sundays.

day_by_day.notes: Anne Frank House tickets sell out weeks or even months ahead — if not already booked, check for last-minute ticket releases at 09:00 Amsterdam time exactly 2 months before your visit date. The canal boat tour and Anne Frank House are within easy walking distance of each other and the hotel, making this a very efficient day.

day_by_day.morning: Free museum morning — Visit the Amsterdam Museum aan de Amstel (formerly Amsterdam Historical Museum) or the Stedelijk Museum (modern art, €20). Alternatively, explore the free Begijnhof — a hidden medieval courtyard garden tucked behind the Spui square, one of Amsterdam's best-kept free secrets. Then walk through the Spui and browse the book market (open Fridays, but the square is lovely any day).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Eastern Docklands (IJburg/NDSM area) or take a free GVB ferry from behind Centraal Station to Amsterdam-Noord. Visit the NDSM Wharf — a massive creative arts hub in a former shipyard with street art, studios, and an alternative vibe. The ferry ride itself offers great views of the IJ waterway. Completely free.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Amsterdam. Visit the Heineken Experience (€23) if interested, or skip to save budget. Walk along the Amstel river at dusk for beautiful canal and bridge views — the Magere Brug (Skinny Bridge) is especially photogenic when lit up at night.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast or grab a croissant and coffee from a local bakery (~€4).
meals.lunch: Lunch at Pllek in Amsterdam-Noord (near NDSM Wharf) — a popular riverside restaurant and beach bar with affordable lunch options (€9–13). Great views of the IJ.
meals.dinner: Toko Joyce or a similar Indonesian restaurant in the city centre — nasi goreng or bami goreng for €10–12. Indonesian cuisine is a beloved Dutch staple thanks to colonial history.

day_by_day.notes: The free GVB ferry to Amsterdam-Noord runs 24/7 and is covered by your transit card. NDSM Wharf is roughly 15 minutes by ferry from Centraal Station. Monday is a good day to visit as weekend crowds have thinned. Check if any free outdoor events or markets are happening around the city.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Hortus Botanicus — one of the oldest botanical gardens in the world (est. 1638), located near Waterlooplein. Beautiful, peaceful, and affordable (€12.50). Spend 1.5 hours among the greenhouses and outdoor gardens. Afterwards, browse the Waterlooplein Flea Market (open Mon–Sat, free entry) for vintage finds and souvenirs at negotiable prices.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final canal exploration — rent a pedal boat or kayak on the canals (Boaty Amsterdam ~€12–15/hour per boat, shared cost) for a DIY canal experience. This is a fun, budget-friendly alternative to a guided tour if you did the boat tour on Day 3. Alternatively, revisit a favourite neighbourhood or pop into the free Scheepvaartmuseum courtyard or the Artis Royal Zoo exterior for photos.
day_by_day.evening: Last evening in Amsterdam — head to Vondelpark for a sunset stroll (Amsterdam's beloved green lung, always free). Then enjoy a farewell dinner in the Leidseplein area before packing for departure.

meals.breakfast: Full Dutch breakfast at the hotel or a nearby grand café — uitsmijter (fried eggs on bread with ham and cheese) ~€8–10.
meals.lunch: Grab a fresh herring sandwich (broodje haring) from a street fish stall near Waterlooplein — the most authentic Amsterdam snack for ~€4–5.
meals.dinner: Brasserie Blazer or a similar mid-range Dutch brasserie near Leidseplein — three-course dagmenu (daily set menu) often available for €22–28. A fitting farewell meal without breaking the budget.

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if your departure flight is in the evening. Amsterdam Centraal to Schiphol by train takes ~17 minutes; trains run every 10–15 minutes. Keep your GVB transit card loaded or buy a single ticket for the airport journey. Leave at least 2.5 hours before your flight for check-in and security.

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival — Flight KL lands at 13:00. No morning activities scheduled. Take the Amsterdam Airport Express (Sprinter) from Schiphol to Amsterdam Centraal (~17 min, €5.40). Check in to Canal House Amsterdam, freshen up, and get oriented in the neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Jordaan Neighborhood Food & Canal Walk — After settling in, take a leisurely self-guided stroll through the iconic Jordaan district. Explore the picturesque canals, browse the boutique shops on Elandsgracht, and soak in the classic Amsterdam atmosphere. Stop at a traditional brown café (bruine kroeg) for a local Heineken or jenever (Dutch gin) to kick off the trip.
day_by_day.evening: Evening Canal Stroll along the Herengracht and Prinsengracht — As the golden hour light hits the canal houses, walk the famous 'Golden Bend' stretch. Dine at a nearby restaurant along the canal for a relaxed first evening.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in-flight or at Schiphol Airport. Try a coffee and stroopwafel at one of the airport cafés.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite near the hotel upon arrival — try Café Papeneiland on Prinsengracht, a historic brown café serving Dutch apple pie and sandwiches (€10–15).
meals.dinner: Toscanini (Lindengracht, Jordaan) — a beloved Italian-Dutch neighborhood restaurant with a warm atmosphere. Expect €25–35 per person for pasta and a glass of wine. Reserve ahead if possible.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. The Jordaan neighborhood is within easy walking distance of Canal House Amsterdam. Pick up an OV-chipkaart (public transit card) at Centraal Station for easy transport throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Rijksmuseum Visit — Arrive at the Rijksmuseum when doors open at 9:00 AM to beat the crowds. Spend 2.5–3 hours exploring the Netherlands' premier museum, including Rembrandt's 'Night Watch,' Vermeer's 'The Milkmaid,' and the stunning Cuypers Library. Book tickets online in advance (€22.50 per person).
day_by_day.afternoon: Van Gogh Museum Experience — Just a 5-minute walk from the Rijksmuseum, the Van Gogh Museum houses the world's largest collection of Van Gogh's works. Explore 'Sunflowers,' 'The Bedroom,' and the moving letters to his brother Theo. Allow 1.5–2 hours. Pre-book tickets (€22 per person). Afterward, relax in the adjacent Vondelpark — Amsterdam's beloved green lung.
day_by_day.evening: Leidseplein Square & surroundings — Head to the lively Leidseplein area for dinner and evening entertainment. Browse the square's café terraces and street performers before settling in for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or at Café Hegeraad (Noordermarkt area) — a classic Amsterdam café offering eggs, toast, and fresh coffee for €8–12.
meals.lunch: Museumplein Café (inside Rijksmuseum garden) or grab a broodje (Dutch sandwich) from a nearby bakery. Budget €10–15.
meals.dinner: Café de Klos (Korsjespoortsteeg) — a rustic, mid-range restaurant famous for its spare ribs and grilled meats. Very popular with locals. Budget €20–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Sunday can be busy at both museums — arriving right at opening is strongly recommended. The Museumplein area is easily walkable from Canal House Amsterdam (~20 min) or take tram 2 or 12.

day_by_day.morning: Anne Frank House Tour — Book the earliest available time slot (tickets sell out weeks in advance — book online at annefrank.org). The experience takes approximately 1–1.5 hours and is profoundly moving. Walk through the hidden annex on Prinsengracht where Anne Frank and her family hid for over two years during WWII. Tickets cost €16 per person.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private Canal Boat Tour — After the emotional morning, unwind with a 1.5–2 hour private canal boat tour through Amsterdam's UNESCO-listed canal ring. Glide past 17th-century merchant houses, narrow bridges, and houseboats. Departs from the Jordaan or Centraal area. Cost is approximately €30–50 per person for a small group tour.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Nine Streets (De 9 Straatjes) — A charming grid of nine small streets connecting the main canals, filled with vintage shops, independent boutiques, and cozy cafés. Perfect for a relaxed evening browse before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Buffet breakfast at the hotel or visit Café Winkel 43 (Noordermarkt) — famous for its apple pie. Grab a coffee and a slice for €5–8.
meals.lunch: Grab lunch after the canal tour at Brouwerij 't IJ — Amsterdam's iconic windmill brewery. Try a craft beer and a light snack (bitterballen, cheese) for €12–18.
meals.dinner: Restaurant Greetje (Peperstraat) — Amsterdam's best traditional Dutch cuisine restaurant. Try stamppot, herring, or Dutch beef stew. Budget €30–40 per person. Reserve in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Anne Frank House tickets are extremely limited — book as far in advance as possible (months ahead). The house is a short walk from Canal House Amsterdam along the Prinsengracht canal. Bring tissues.

day_by_day.morning: Albert Cuyp Market & De Pijp Neighborhood — Take tram 24 to Amsterdam's most famous street market, the Albert Cuyp Markt (open Mon–Sat, 9:00–17:00). Browse 300+ stalls selling fresh stroopwafels, raw herring (haring), Dutch cheeses, flowers, and clothing. Explore the vibrant De Pijp neighborhood surrounding it — one of Amsterdam's most multicultural and lively areas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Foam Photography Museum & Rembrandtplein — Visit the Foam Photography Museum on Keizersgracht, one of Europe's leading photography museums with rotating world-class exhibitions (€15 entry). Afterward, walk to Rembrandtplein square to see the bronze statue of Rembrandt and the lively café terraces.
day_by_day.evening: Canal-side sunset drinks and dinner in the Jordaan — Return to the Jordaan for a relaxed evening. Find a canal-side bench or café terrace for golden hour drinks before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or visit Bakers & Roasters (Eerste Jacob van Campenstraat, De Pijp) — a New Zealand-inspired brunch café with excellent eggs and smoothies. Budget €12–18.
meals.lunch: Eat at the Albert Cuyp Market itself — grab a fresh haring (raw herring with onions, €4), stroopwafel (€2), and Dutch fries (patat) with mayonnaise (€4). A delicious and very affordable market lunch under €15.
meals.dinner: Moeder's (Rozengracht, Jordaan) — a beloved local restaurant decorated with family photos brought by guests. Serves hearty Dutch home-style cooking. Budget €20–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Albert Cuyp Market is closed on Sundays, so Tuesday is ideal. De Pijp is about 20 minutes by tram from the hotel. The Foam Museum is relatively uncrowded on weekday afternoons — a great hidden gem for photography enthusiasts.

day_by_day.morning: Amsterdam Centraal & Waterfront (NDSM Wharf or Eastern Docklands) — Take the free ferry from behind Centraal Station across the IJ river to explore Amsterdam Noord, a creative hub with street art, the EYE Film Museum (stunning architecture, free entry to the building), and the A'DAM Lookout tower (€17.50 for panoramic views of the city). A perfect final morning perspective of Amsterdam from above.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute Canal Walk & Souvenir Shopping — Return to the city center for a final leisurely walk along the Herengracht and Singel canals. Stop at the Bloemenmarkt (floating flower market on the Singel) to pick up tulip bulbs or Delftware as souvenirs. Visit a local cheese shop (like Henri Willig) for Dutch Gouda to take home.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner in the Jordaan — End the trip with a special dinner at one of Amsterdam's finest canal-side restaurants before preparing for departure.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast or visit Lot Sixty One Coffee Roasters (Kinkerstraat) — Amsterdam's best specialty coffee spot with excellent pastries. Budget €8–12.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at EYE Film Museum café on the waterfront — sandwiches and soups with stunning views of the IJ river and Amsterdam skyline. Budget €12–16.
meals.dinner: Rijsel (Marcusstraat) — a beautifully designed restaurant in a former gymnasium, known for its rotisserie chicken and French-Belgian-Dutch menu. A memorable farewell dinner. Budget €30–40 per person. Reserve ahead.

day_by_day.notes: The free ferry to Amsterdam Noord runs 24/7 and departs every few minutes from behind Centraal Station — a quintessential Amsterdam experience. Pack bags the night before if flying out on Day 6. Keep receipts for any VAT refund if eligible. The OV-chipkaart can be refunded at Schiphol or Centraal Station before departure.

trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival — Flight KL lands at 13:00. No morning activities scheduled. Transfer from Amsterdam Airport Schiphol to Canal House Amsterdam via private chauffeur service (pre-arranged luxury transfer, approx. 30–40 minutes). Check in, freshen up, and settle into your canal-view suite.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private Canal Boat Tour — After settling in, embark on a private guided canal boat tour departing from a nearby jetty on the Herengracht. Glide through Amsterdam's UNESCO-listed canal ring, passing iconic 17th-century merchant houses, hidden gardens, and historic drawbridges. Your private skipper will narrate the Golden Age history of the city. Duration: approximately 2 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Herengracht and Keizersgracht at dusk to experience the famous 'Magic Hour' when the canal lights reflect on the water. Enjoy a relaxed first evening dinner at a top canal-side restaurant.

meals.lunch: Light welcome spread arranged by Canal House Amsterdam upon arrival, or a quick stop at Dignita Hoftuin for artisan sandwiches and fresh juices near the hotel
meals.dinner: Dinner at Vinkeles — a Michelin-starred restaurant set inside a beautifully restored 18th-century bakery within the Dylan Hotel, offering contemporary French-Dutch cuisine with an exceptional wine list. Reserve the chef's tasting menu for a memorable first evening.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange your private airport transfer before departure. Contact Canal House Amsterdam concierge in advance to book the private canal boat tour for the afternoon slot (14:30–16:30 recommended). Vinkeles requires advance reservation — book at least 2–3 weeks ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Rijksmuseum Visit — Begin the day with a premium, skip-the-line private guided tour of the Rijksmuseum, the Netherlands' premier art and history museum. Spend 2.5–3 hours exploring masterpieces by Rembrandt (The Night Watch), Vermeer (The Milkmaid), and Delft Blue porcelain collections. A private guide will provide deep historical and artistic context tailored to your interests.
day_by_day.afternoon: Van Gogh Museum Experience — A short walk from the Rijksmuseum, dive into the world's largest collection of Van Gogh's works. Discover Sunflowers, The Bedroom, and Almond Blossom across chronological galleries. Book a premium timed-entry or private after-hours access if available. Spend approximately 2 hours. Afterwards, take a leisurely walk through Vondelpark, Amsterdam's elegant central park, just steps away.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel to refresh, then enjoy an evening exploring the elegant Negen Straatjes (Nine Streets) boutique shopping district before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel — Canal House Amsterdam offers a curated in-house breakfast; alternatively, visit Bakers & Roasters nearby for a premium brunch spread with specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café Cobra, located directly across from the Rijksmuseum on Museumplein — a stylish brasserie with seasonal Dutch dishes and excellent salads in a bright, airy setting
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ciel Bleu — Amsterdam's celebrated two-Michelin-starred restaurant on the 23rd floor of Hotel Okura, offering panoramic city views and a world-class French-Japanese fusion tasting menu with an award-winning wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: Book Rijksmuseum private guided tours through their official site or a luxury concierge service. Van Gogh Museum timed-entry tickets sell out weeks in advance — secure these before your trip. Ciel Bleu reservations should be made 4–6 weeks in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Anne Frank House Tour — A profoundly moving and essential Amsterdam experience. Visit the hidden annex where Anne Frank and her family hid during World War II. Book a premium early-morning timed-entry slot (8:00–9:00 AM) to experience the house with fewer crowds. Allow 1.5–2 hours for a reflective, unhurried visit. The house is located in the Jordaan neighborhood, a short walk from the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Jordaan Neighborhood Food & Canal Walk — Transition from the weight of the morning into the charm of the Jordaan. Join a premium private food and canal walking tour through Amsterdam's most picturesque neighborhood. Stop at traditional brown cafes (bruine kroegen) for Dutch jenever (gin), sample artisan cheeses, stroopwafels, and herring at local specialty shops, and admire the hidden courtyards (hofjes) and flower-lined canals unique to this district.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks aboard a private electric boat rented for the evening — cruise the Jordaan canals with a bottle of champagne as the city lights come on. Return to the hotel and enjoy a refined dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before the Anne Frank House opening slot — opt for the full Dutch breakfast with cold cuts, artisan cheeses, fresh bread, and coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Winkel 43 in the Jordaan, famous for its legendary apple pie, followed by a cheese tasting at Fromagerie Abraham Kef, one of Amsterdam's finest artisan cheese shops
meals.dinner: Dinner at De Kas — a stunning restaurant set inside a 1926 greenhouse in Frankendael Park. Farm-to-table Mediterranean-Dutch cuisine where nearly everything is grown on-site. A unique and romantic luxury dining experience

day_by_day.notes: Anne Frank House tickets are extremely limited and must be booked online weeks in advance — no walk-in tickets are available. The private electric boat for the evening can be arranged through your hotel concierge or companies like Mokumboot or Those Dam Boat Guys.

day_by_day.morning: Day Excursion — Keukenhof Gardens & Dutch Countryside (if open, Keukenhof typically runs mid-March to mid-May — confirm 2027 dates). If available, arrange a private chauffeured trip to Keukenhof, the world's largest flower garden, just 30km from Amsterdam. Walk through 32 hectares of blooming tulips, hyacinths, and daffodils in peak spring color. Alternatively, if Keukenhof has closed for the season, visit the charming windmill village of Zaanse Schans for an authentic Dutch countryside experience with private guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Amsterdam by early afternoon. Visit the Hermitage aan de Amstel or the Amsterdam Museum (check current exhibitions) for a curated cultural afternoon. Alternatively, explore the Stedelijk Museum for world-class modern and contemporary art — a perfect complement to the classical art seen at the Rijksmuseum.
day_by_day.evening: Leisure evening — explore the upscale P.C. Hooftstraat (Amsterdam's luxury shopping street) for designer boutiques including Louis Vuitton, Chanel, and Gucci. Enjoy cocktails at the iconic Bar Americain inside the Marriott or the rooftop bar at Sir Adam Hotel before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a takeaway from Scandinavian Embassy, one of Amsterdam's finest specialty coffee roasters, with house-baked pastries
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch prepared by the hotel or a local deli enjoyed at Keukenhof Gardens or Vondelpark — ask the concierge to arrange a premium picnic basket with Dutch cheeses, charcuterie, wine, and fresh bread
meals.dinner: Dinner at Rijks Restaurant — the acclaimed restaurant inside the Rijksmuseum itself, helmed by a Michelin-starred team. Dutch-inspired contemporary cuisine in a stunning museum setting with exceptional seasonal ingredients

day_by_day.notes: Verify Keukenhof's 2027 closing date before finalizing this day. Private chauffeur for the countryside excursion can be booked through the hotel or services like Blacklane. Rijks Restaurant reservations should be secured well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning — sleep in and enjoy a long, indulgent breakfast at the hotel. Take a peaceful solo walk along the Herengracht and Prinsengracht canals, stopping to admire the canal houses and floating flower market (Bloemenmarkt) on the Singel. Pick up premium Dutch souvenirs: tulip bulbs, aged Gouda, Delft Blue ceramics, or Dutch gin from a specialty shop.
